title: What If Earth Stopped Spinning for 1 Second?
alt_titles: Earth Stops Spinning for ONE Second. Here's the Real Math
1 Second Without Earth's Spin: Mach 1.37 Winds, Tsunamis & More
description:
Right now Earth's spin carries you at up to 1,670 km/h (465 m/s). What if, for one second, the ground stopped and nothing else did?

We run the scenario through real physics and show every calculation on screen: the supersonic wind, the shear wave through every building, water hammer on the coasts, ocean-wide tsunamis, the restart, and the one permanent change (Earth ends up exactly one second late).

⏱ Chapters
0:00 Intro
0:13 How fast are we spinning?
1:29 The rules
1:56 Second zero: you

7:53 Second one: the restart
8:27 Earth is one second late

🧮 The numbers (computed in code, rounded)
• Equator speed: 2πR ÷ T(sidereal) = 465 m/s ≈ 1,670 km/h
• Wind if the ground stops: Mach 1.37, ram pressure ≥ 132 kPa (≈ 44× a minimum Cat-5 wind)
• Your kinetic energy at the equator (70 kg): 7.6 MJ ≈ 1.8 kg TNT ≈ the energy of a 11 km fall
• Shear wave in steel: τ = ρ c Δv ≈ 12 GPa ≈ 80× shear yield
• Water hammer: Δp = ρ c Δv ≈ 720 MPa, more than 6× the Challenger Deep pressure
• Tsunami speed √(g·d) at 3.7 km depth: 684 km/h
• Rotation lost: 15 arcseconds = 1 leap second
